chapter: Charley Johnson and the Army band
title: Army band and Lieutenant Bill Vodery
summary: Wooding says he was a second-class musician in the band led by Bill Vodery, Ziegfeld's arranger.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And what was your function in the Army?
Well, I was a -- I started in as a Third

and ended up as a Second Class musician. I played in the band. But, I wasn't any kind of non-commissioned officer for the simple reason why, every day I was in the Y.M.C.A. practicing, playing. And I was also watching my friend I took so much off of. Old Bill Vodey. Old Bill Vodey was the rage for Ziegfeld. He was a man that came from Philadelphia. But he done quite a lot of arranging. He was such an arranger, that for some time, George Gershwin worked in his office as a copyist.
He was the leader of the military band that you were in?

Right, he was lieutenant. Bill Vodery. He took the examination in CHAUMONT and he was supposed to have two hours to do it, he did it in twenty minutes. Because he'd been on Broadway, working with Ziegfeld. So that's what happened.
